## Natural history notes

A medium-sized tropical cockroach characterized by its flattened oval body, long antennae, brown to reddish-brown coloration, and pale-edged pronotum that can give it a banded or shielded appearance. In Florida, it has been recorded in warm, humid habitats and is especially associated with wet areas such as streams, ditches, and moist vegetation, where it may shelter in leaf litter or debris. It feeds on decaying plant material and other organic matter, and unlike household pest roaches, it is more of an outdoor detritivore; members of this species are notable for entering water when disturbed and being able to swim or remain submerged for short periods.
